name: Susan Serves Dessert at the Dinner Gathering
description: Susan entered the dining area carrying dessert plates and distributed them to the guests seated around the table. She placed a plate in front of Viviers, who sat without a companion, and then served Minister Dominee Bester and his wife. The table bore the remains of the earlier courses—tapered candles pooled in wax, wineglasses smeared with residue, and a tablecloth stained with food, wine, and ash. The school's headmaster, Cloete, and his wife were also present, continuing their conversation as dessert was set before them.

description: At the end of the workday, Ben and Cloete stood by their cars in the car park. Ben told Cloete not to worry, saying he wasn't a crusader and that he'd known Gordon a long time. Cloete replied that he understood, calling it Ben's Christian duty to his neighbor. Ben agreed, saying something like that. Cloete warned him not to get too close, adding that teachers must stay out of politics. He said he loved to Susan, then got into his car and drove off. description: In the carpeted offices of a Johannesburg law firm, a black woman finishes her early-morning cleaning and packs up her supplies. White staff arrive, bright and well-dressed, removing covers from typewriters and settling at their desks. A young black girl, neatly dressed and carrying a tray of coffee, moves from desk to desk, delivering cups. description: In the sparsely furnished charge office, a long bench runs along one wall. Sergeant Van Zyl stands behind the reception counter with Captain Stolz, a tall blond man with a scar on his chin. A group of boys lines up against the wall. Van Zyl calls out each boy's name and looks to Stolz. When Stolz nods, the boy steps aside. Those selected are marched to a waiting police van and driven away. The remaining boys, including Jonathan and Wellington, are taken to the cells at the police station.

name: Ben Supervises a History Test
description: Afrikaans boys in uniform hunch over their desks, writing quietly during a history test. On the blackboard, the date and exam questions are written: the arrival of the first white man in South Africa, the Battle of Blood River, the Zulu chief defeated at Isandlwana, the president of the first Afrikander Republic, and the route of the Voortrekkers from the Cape. Ben walks slowly between the rows, watching the students. He pauses occasionally to look out the window at Gordon's tractor, sitting still in the field. One boy stares at the ceiling, pen in his mouth, struggling. Ben smiles, steps over, bends down beside him in the same posture. The class erupts in laughter. Ben stands, slaps the boy’s back, and announces, 'All right, time up! Hand in your test.' The students groan as they pass in their papers.

He asks if there are any other lists or places they should check, insisting there must be more information. The sergeant shakes his head, repeating that the person is not in custody, and suggests they try the hospital or the mortuary. Gordon inhales sharply at the word 'mortuary.' Stanley, undeterred, asks about John Voster Square. The sergeant replies that he has already tried to help. Stanley steps away and approaches a woman waiting nearby, asking who she is looking for. She says they took her 13-year-old girl. He offers quiet comfort just as the officer calls her to the counter.

Without warning, Captain Stolz steps forward and punches Gordon hard in the face. Gordon collapses to the floor, blood pouring from his nose and mouth. description: Susan carried salads out to the garden, placing them on the table. Chris stood by the barbecue, squinting as smoke rose into his eyes. Ben bounced little Hennie in a small portable pool, the water splashing with each gentle lift. The black nanny sat nearby in the shade, a towel resting in her lap, ready. The family moved through the afternoon in quiet rhythm until Gordon and Jonathan appeared at the far side of the garden. Gordon stood with his hat pressed to his chest, Jonathan beside him, posture stiff. The activity slowed. Susan looked up first, then Chris, then Ben. After a pause, Ben stepped forward, walking toward them.

Ben, visibly relieved, thanked Viljoen and made for the door. Before leaving, he accepted Viljoen's message of regards to his father-in-law, with a promise to pass it on. Ben stepped out, the door closing behind him. For a moment, the room was silent. Viljoen stood still, watching the door. Then he turned to Stolz, who had been waiting, and asked, 'Is the little bird singing yet?' Stolz replied, 'I'm working on it.' Viljoen nodded. Stolz left, shutting the door behind him.

After a pause, Stanley breaks the quiet, asking, "What now?" Gordon responds, "He is our son... we must find him." Julius says he will make more inquiries, mentioning John Vorster Square and the special branch, though he admits he doesn't hold out much hope. Gordon reminds him, "You're a lawyer, Julius!" Stanley laughs bitterly, saying, "A black lawyer! Those Boers... the bastards'll kick him around till they lose him." Emily suggests asking the Baas for help, but Gordon replies bitterly that the Baas did nothing when the boy was flogged and is unlikely to help now.

related_events: Stanley greets Wellington and his companions
Wellington approaches Stanley's car with a limp

name: Wellington's Scar
description: After Wellington gets into the car and takes off his sunglasses, Stanley sees a deep scar running from his forehead to his cheek and reacts with concern. Gordon asks if the injury was caused by others. Wellington responds with a nervous twitch in his arm and silently nods.
related_events: Stanley observes Wellington's facial scar
Gordon inquires about the cause of Wellington's injury
Wellington confirms injury origin with a nod

name: Gordon Learns of Jonathan's Death
description: Gordon asks Wellington about Jonathan, wanting to know if he has been released or how he is doing. Wellington says he last saw Jonathan weeks ago and doesn’t know what happened to him. Stanley then tells Gordon that Jonathan is dead. Gordon, hearing this, insists on knowing how Jonathan died.
related_events: Gordon inquires about Jonathan's fate
Wellington recalls last seeing Jonathan weeks ago
Stanley informs Gordon of Jonathan's death

name: Ben Completes Registration at Security Desk
description: Ben arrives at a secure facility and fills out an entry slip at a security desk. A uniformed policeman observes him from inside a bulletproof glass cage. After Ben hands over the slip, the policeman makes a phone call. While waiting, Ben notices a video surveillance camera. Another officer brings in a 20-year-old African girl with Afro-style hair, escorted by two white policemen. They lead her into a lift, and Ben watches as the lift ascends to the 10th floor. The policeman stamps Ben's slip and returns it to him. A moment later, the policeman tells Ben that someone will meet him on the second floor. Ben enters the lift.
related_events: Ben fills out an entry slip at a security desk
Policeman makes a phone call after receiving Ben's slip
Policeman stamps Ben's slip and returns it

name: Ben watches a girl being taken to the 10th floor
description: After handing in a slip through a bulletproof glass cage, Ben waits under the watch of a uniformed policeman. He notices a video surveillance camera in the area. A 20-year-old African girl with Afro-style hair is brought in, held on both sides by two white policemen. They lead her into a lift. Ben watches as the lift ascends to the 10th floor. The policeman stamps Ben's slip and tells him someone will meet him on the second floor. Ben enters a lift.
related_events: Ben notices a video surveillance camera in the area
Two policemen escort an African girl into the building
Escorted girl is taken into a lift by two policemen
Ben observes the lift's movement to the 10th floor

name: Ben Takes the Elevator to the Second Floor
description: The policeman stamped the slip and handed it back to Ben. 'Somebody will meet you on second floor,' he said. Ben turned and walked to the elevator, stepped inside, and pressed the button for the second floor.
related_events: Policeman informs Ben that someone will meet him on the second floor
Ben enters a lift to go to the second floor

name: Gordon Demands the Truth About Jonathan's Death
description: Gordon stands with Ben on the edge of the playing fields as the sounds of a school rugby match fade in the background. He speaks with growing intensity, insisting that knowing how his son Jonathan died is not something he can let go. He rejects the official story, saying it brings him no peace. Ben places a hand on Gordon’s shoulder, offering sympathy and reminding him he still has other children to live for. Gordon interrupts, pressing for the truth—how Jonathan died and where his body lies. He declares that his son belongs to him and Emily, and that he will not stop until he knows what happened. Without waiting for a reply, Gordon climbs onto his lawnmower, starts the engine, and drives across the field, leaving Ben behind. From an office window in the school, the headmaster watches the scene unfold, concerned.
related_events: Gordon expresses grief and moral urgency to Ben
Ben responds to Gordon with resignation and comfort
Gordon interrupts Ben to demand truth about his son's death

name: Gordon Takes the Lawnmower
description: After speaking with Ben, Gordon climbs onto the lawnmower parked at the edge of the field. He starts the engine, the sound cutting through the air. Without another word, he drives across the playing fields, leaving Ben behind. The lawnmower moves slowly over the grass, heading away from the school and the voices calling after him.
related_events: Gordon starts lawnmower engine and drives across playing fields

name: Cloete Watches Gordon Leave
description: From his office window, Headmaster Cloete watches Gordon drive away on the lawnmower across the field. The rugby game has ended, and the boys have run off. Ben remains standing alone, looking after Gordon. Cloete speaks, his voice low and concerned, warning Ben to be careful, reminding him that these are not normal times and that one must make allowances.
related_events: Headmaster Cloete observes from office window and issues warning to Ben

name: Rugby Game Ends as Gordon Confronts Ben
description: On the playing fields, two teams of schoolboys in crisp uniforms play a rugby match, their shouts and the shrill of whistles rising into the still, warm air. The game unfolds with precision and energy, drawing attention from the surrounding grounds. A final whistle pierces the atmosphere, signaling the end. The boys scramble off the field, running past Ben and Gordon, who stand nearby. The noise of the game fades as the players disappear, leaving the two men in quiet confrontation. Gordon turns away, climbs onto a lawnmower parked at the edge of the field, and starts the engine. Ben calls out to him, but Gordon remains resolute. The mower chugs to life, and he drives slowly across the grass, leaving Ben standing alone.
related_events: Schoolboy rugby game takes place on playing fields
Schoolboy rugby game ends with a whistle

name: Man in Blue Overalls Demands Silence Amid Rising Tension
description: In the crowded third-class carriage, a large woman shouts at a man to watch where his bag is swinging. Laughter spreads as passengers exchange teasing remarks. One man jokes that modern electricity keeps people from turning off the lights, prompting more laughter. A woman near Gordon mocks his thick glasses, saying he wouldn’t be able to see anything anyway. Another man chimes in, asking if his wife wears thick glasses too. The first man fires back, “You should know, she’s your sister,” and the carriage erupts in laughter again. Then, a man in blue overalls suddenly jumps onto his seat, waving his arms. “Quiet! Thulani! Thulani!” he shouts. The noise dies down. “They are killing our children and you are making jokes,” he says. A voice from somewhere adds, “They say hundreds of children have died and Soweto is burning.”
related_events: Large woman confronts man about his bag in crowded carriage
Passengers react with laughter to escalating banter
Man jokes about electricity and intimacy
Woman teases Gordon about his glasses
Man retorts that another man knows his wife's glasses
Man in blue overalls stands and demands silence

name: The Carriage Falls Silent
description: The man in blue overalls jumps onto his seat, waving his arms and shouting, 'Quiet! Thulani! Thulani!' The laughter and chatter in the carriage die down. He glares at the passengers and says, 'They are killing our children and you are making jokes.' An off-screen voice adds, 'They say hundreds of children have died and Soweto is burning.' Gordon and a woman near him exchange glances, absorbing the news. A smartly-dressed man mutters, 'The white people, they will pay, and soon.' A young woman speaks up sharply, 'They will pay, they will pay. Since when have they been killing us, putting us in jails, starving our children to death, taking our land? Hundreds of years. And what have you men done? Only talk, talk, talk. You are not men. Sis.' Her words hang in the air. The mood in the carriage shifts. The jokes stop. No one answers.
related_events: Man in blue overalls accuses others of ignoring violence against children
Off-screen voice reports mass child deaths and Soweto uprising
Young woman challenges men's inaction and masculinity

name: The Train Arrives in Soweto Amid Smoke and Fire
description: The train rolls into Soweto, and through the windows, thick smoke rises from several areas of the township. Flames engulf official buildings, including the superintendent's office. Passengers press against the windows, murmuring in low, tense voices. 'That's the superintendent's office on fire,' someone says. Another voice: 'I hope the children are home.' A smartly-dressed man clenches his fists and says, 'The white people, they will pay, and soon.' Others nod or mutter in agreement. A woman adds, 'I hope the world hears about this.' The mood in the carriage turns heavy, alert, as people brace for what awaits them outside.
related_events: Train arrives in Soweto amid visible destruction and fire
Smartly-dressed man declares white people will pay
Passengers react with fear and urgency to unfolding crisis

name: Ben and Emily Exit School to Meet Stanley
description: The school bell rings, signaling the end of the tea interval. Ben and Emily leave the school grounds and walk toward Stanley's car, where Stanley has been waiting. He is sitting in the car wearing sunglasses. As they approach, Stanley gets out and stands by the vehicle.
related_events: School bell signals end of tea interval
Stanley waits in his car for Ben and Emily
Ben and Emily walk out to meet Stanley

name: Stanley Greets Ben and Emily Explains His Role
description: Stanley gets out of his car and walks over to Ben, extending his hand. 'How's it? I'm Stanley! I heard about you!' he says. Ben hesitates, seeming a little uneasy. Emily steps in, 'This is Stanley Makhaya... He helps us all the time.' Stanley then opens the car door for Emily. 'Don't worry too much, Emily, I'm sure Gordon will be home in a few days,' Ben says. With a loud laugh, Stanley slaps the car door shut and gets into the driver's seat. He starts the car and drives away. Ben stands still, looking puzzled.
related_events: Stanley exits car and greets Ben
Emily introduces Stanley Makhaya to Ben

name: Ben Reassures Emily as Stanley Departs Abruptly
description: Ben tells Emily not to worry, saying he is sure Gordon will be home in a few days. Stanley laughs, slaps the car door shut, gets into the driver's seat, and drives away. Ben stands still, watching the car leave, a look of confusion on his face.
related_events: Ben reassures Emily about Gordon's return
Stanley slams car door and departs laughing

name: Ben Watches Stanley Drive Away
description: Ben stands still as Stanley gets into the car and drives off. The camera focuses on Ben’s face, where a look of confusion settles as he watches the car disappear. He remains silent, his expression unreadable, the moment stretching before he finally looks away.
related_events: Ben shows perplexed expression as Stanley leaves

name: Youths Storm Beer Hall with Protest
description: A group of about twenty youths enters the beer hall and moves through the drinking area, where men are seated on long benches drinking from plastic containers. The leader of the group steps forward and addresses the patrons, shouting that their children are starving while they drink, and demands an end to the beer hall gatherings. He declares that revolution and drinking cannot coexist and calls for a boycott of the beer halls. The patrons, some visibly drunk, react angrily. A large man with sideburns rises from his seat, brandishing a stick, and demands to know since when children are allowed to speak this way to their fathers. He and several others advance toward the youths. The boys retreat, running into the serving area, closing the doors behind them, and begin breaking things inside.
related_events: Group of youths enters beer hall to protest drinking
Leader of youth group delivers protest speech to patrons
related_occasions: Beer Hall Gathering

name: Drunk Patron Confronts Youths After Protest Speech
description: After the youth leader speaks out against drinking and calls for a boycott of the beer hall, a man with sideburns, clearly drunk, stands up and shouts that children have no right to speak to their fathers that way, declaring they need a beating. He raises a stick and moves forward with several other men toward the group of youths. The boys back away, then turn and run into the serving area, closing the doors behind them. From inside, the sound of breaking objects begins to emerge as the men approach the closed doors.
related_events: Drunk man with sideburns challenges youth leader's authority
Patrons advance on youths in response to protest
Youths retreat to serving area and begin destroying property
related_occasions: Beer Hall Gathering

name: Police Arrive and Arrest Youths at Beer Hall
description: Two police Land Rovers screech to a halt outside the beer hall. The group of youths who had taken refuge inside rush out through a side entrance and run down the street. Jonathan and Wellington, walking toward the beer hall, see the boys fleeing and the police chasing them. As they turn to run, a second Land Rover pulls up, blocking their escape. Police officers, two black and two white, converge on the scene. Jonathan, Wellington, and about ten of the fleeing boys are grabbed, hauled to the ground, and forced into the vehicle. They shout that they are not involved, but the officers ignore their protests. The Land Rovers drive away, carrying the arrested youths.
related_events: Two police Land Rovers arrive at beer hall and boys flee through side entrance
Jonathan and Wellington encounter fleeing boys and pursuing police
Additional police Land Rover blocks escape route
Jonathan, Wellington, and approximately ten boys are arrested by mixed-race police unit
Arrested youths are forced into police vehicle and driven away
related_occasions: Beer Hall Gathering

name: Interrogation and Intimidation of Gordon
description: Gordon stands facing the wall, his arms raised. His trousers are wet. Captain Stolz paces behind him. When Gordon tries to speak, explaining he has done nothing and was only trying to find something, Stolz hits him in the face. Lieutenant Venter, seated on the edge of a desk, smokes quietly. He orders Gordon to keep his arms up. When Gordon lowers them, Venter snaps at him to raise them again. Venter then walks over, removes his cigarette from his mouth, and calmly stubs it on Gordon's neck before returning to his spot. Gordon remains silent, his body tense, showing no further response to their demands.
related_events: Captain Stolz demands information from Gordon
Gordon pleads innocence to interrogation officers
Captain Stolz strikes Gordon in the face
Lieutenant Venter orders Gordon to raise his arms
Gordon stands with raised arm facing the wall
Gordon wets his trousers out of fear

name: Lieutenant Venter Stubs Cigarette on Gordon's Neck
description: Lieutenant Venter walks slowly to Gordon, removes the cigarette from his lips, and calmly stubs it on Gordon's neck. He then returns to his place by the desk. Gordon remains silent.
related_events: Lieutenant Venter questions Gordon about not answering Captain Stolz
Lieutenant Venter stubs cigarette on Gordon's neck
Gordon remains silent after accusation of receiving information

name: Gordon is subjected to wet bag torture
description: Captain Stolz calls out for Johannes. A black security policeman enters carrying a bag. He walks to a bucket in the corner and soaks the bag in water. Lieutenant Venter grabs Gordon, forces him onto a chair, and handcuffs his hands behind it. Under Captain Stolz's supervision, Venter places the wet bag over Gordon's head and ties it securely. Gordon begins to groan and wriggle.
related_events: Captain Stolz calls for Johannes and the bag
Johannes the security policeman enters with a bag
Johannes wets the bag in a bucket
Lieutenant Venter places wet bag over Gordon's head and ties it
Captain Stolz supervises the interrogation procedure

name: Stanley and Julius Lead Parents into Morgue for Identification
description: A white-uniformed assistant opens the door to a cool, sterile room lined with metal drawers. He leads a group of African parents down the center aisle. Stanley and Julius, a black lawyer, walk among them, shaking hands with some, receiving quiet salutes from others. Gordon and Emily follow closely, their faces drawn with grief and anger. Stanley places a large hand gently on Emily's shoulder as they stop before the first drawer. The assistant pulls it open, revealing the face of a dead child—some bodies are clothed in torn, dirty garments, others are naked, some show wounds, others appear whole except for small, neat holes in their temples or chests, marked by dried blood. A woman behind them lets out a scream, collapsing against a drawer. Another woman rushes to hold her as the assistant steps over, listens, then writes a name on a tag and ties it to the child’s wrist. The grieving mother resists being pulled away, her friend wrapping an arm around her waist to lead her back. Other women reach out as they pass. Gordon moves to the last drawer, peers inside, and finds it is not his son. He turns and follows Emily out, past rows of parents and a group of women sitting in silence.
related_events: Assistant leads parents into examination room
Parents identify bodies of deceased children
Stanley comforts Emily during identification process
related_occasions: Body Identification Session At Morgue

name: A Mother's Grief in the Morgue
description: A woman lets out a piercing scream as she recognizes her child in one of the open drawers. She collapses, clutching the edge, her legs giving way beneath her. A friend rushes to her side, wrapping an arm around her, then gently pulls her back from the drawer. The white-uniformed assistant steps forward, listens to a whispered confirmation, and writes a name on a tag, which he ties to the child’s body. The crowd parts silently as the two women move away, the grieving mother barely able to walk. Other women seated nearby reach out as they pass, touching her arm, her shoulder, offering quiet contact as she is led away.
related_events: Woman collapses in grief upon identifying her child's body
Friend physically pulls grieving mother away from her child's body
Assistant tags body after confirmation from grieving parent
Crowd of mourners makes way for grieving mother and friend
Other mourning women reach out to comfort grieving mother
related_occasions: Body Identification Session At Morgue

name: Gordon Confirms Jonathan Is Not Among the Dead
description: Gordon peers into the last metal drawer. The small face inside is not Jonathan's. He steps back, silent. Stanley and Julius move toward the exit, followed by Gordon and Emily. They walk past rows of parents still hunched before open drawers, past a group of women seated on the floor, heads bowed, hands clasped. The air is heavy with breath and silence. No one speaks as they make their way out of the room.
related_events: Gordon confirms Jonathan's absence in final body drawer
Group exits morgue after identification session concludes
related_occasions: Body Identification Session At Morgue

name: Ben Remembers Jonathan's Whipping
description: Ben sits alone in his study, hunched over his desk with a newspaper in front of him. The room is dimly lit by a single desk lamp. He smokes heavily from his pipe, the smoke curling around his head. His shirt is unbuttoned, his jacket draped over the back of his chair. As he stares blankly at the page, Gordon’s voice fills his thoughts, repeating the words: 'That day, Mister Ben, sir, when they whipped Jonathan, you also said we can do nothing. God as my witness today: I must know what happened and where he lies. His body belongs to Emily and me.' Ben mutters under his breath, 'Jeezus -- Jeezus -- Jeezus Christ.'
related_events: Ben reflects on past injustice while smoking in his study

name: Johan Says Good Night
description: Johan enters his father's study, knocking gently on the half-open door. He is wearing pajamas and a dressing gown, ready for bed. Ben looks up from his desk and, without speaking, suddenly pulls his son into a tight embrace, holding him closely. Johan responds by wrapping his arms around his father's neck. After a moment, he pulls back slightly. Ben tells him to go and get some sleep. Johan nods and leaves the room.
related_events: Johan says good night to his father
Ben embraces his son tightly upon saying good night

name: Susan Brings Coffee and Comforts Ben
description: Susan enters Ben's study holding a cup of coffee. She pauses as she sees Ben hugging their son Johan, who is in his pajamas and dressing gown. After a moment, she sets the coffee on the desk and says it's time for Johan to go to bed. Ben agrees, and Johan leaves. Susan tells Ben she's proud of what he's done for the family, then gently strokes his hair and suggests he come to bed soon. He tells her he'll stay a little longer to finish his thoughts. She smiles slightly and leaves him alone in the study.
related_events: Susan brings coffee to Ben in his study
Susan expresses pride in Ben's actions for the family
Susan leaves Ben alone in the study

name: Ben Preserves His Thoughts on Standar Six
description: After Susan leaves, Ben sits at his desk and picks up a cup of coffee. He takes a moment to reflect, then removes a photocopied letter from an envelope and reads it. Setting it aside, he prepares to write, determined to record his thoughts about Standar Six before going to bed.
related_events: Ben decides to preserve thoughts about Standar Six

name: Ben reads the letter about Jonathan Ngubene
description: Ben takes a photocopied letter from an envelope and reads it under the glow of the desk lamp. The letter, typed on official paper, states that there is no record of anyone named Jonathan Ngubene. He sits still for a moment, the paper in his hands, the smoke from his pipe curling into the air. Outside, the house is quiet.
related_events: Ben reads a photocopied letter about Jonathan Ngubene's disappearance

name: Johan Wins the Relay Race
description: Johan races the final leg of the relay, neck-and-neck with another runner, and crosses the finish line just ahead. Students flood the field, cheering and surrounding him. His father, Ben du Toit, pushes through the crowd to reach him, pats him on the back, and tells him it was his best race. Johan, breathless and excited, says he beat the other boy. Ben agrees proudly, then leads him off the field toward the school buildings, where teammates slap Johan on the back. Along the way, Ben stops briefly to instruct Gordon, the gardener, about weeding the marigolds and watering the lawn. Gordon assures him the work will be done, and his son Jonathan will help. Ben asks Jonathan how his algebra is, and Jonathan replies it's still a little difficult. Johan adds that he also finds it hard. Gordon straightens up and says Jonathan is working hard, and their family is grateful for Ben's support. Ben nods and walks away with Johan.
related_events: Johan wins the final leg of the relay race
Students and spectators celebrate Johan's race victory
related_occasions: Dan Pienaar School Athletics Event

name: Ben Assigns Gordon Gardening Work and Checks on Jonathan's Studies
description: After the relay race, Ben du Toit approaches Gordon Ngubene, who is working in the school garden. Ben tells him about the day's tasks—mainly weeding the marigolds and watering the lawn and flowers. Gordon assures him they will be done. Noticing Jonathan standing nearby, Ben asks the boy how he is doing with algebra. Jonathan replies respectfully that it is still a little difficult. Johan, Ben's son, adds that he also finds it tough. Gordon straightens up and says his son is working hard, and that Ben’s support with money and education will not be wasted. Ben nods and says he will see them later, then walks off with his son. Gordon returns to his work a short distance away.
related_events: Ben du Toit assigns gardening tasks to Gordon Ngubene
Ben du Toit checks on Jonathan's algebra progress
Gordon Ngubene expresses gratitude for Ben du Toit's support
related_occasions: Dan Pienaar School Athletics Event

name: Students Trip Jonathan, Sparking Confrontation
description: A group of students laughing and shoving each other approached Jonathan. As they passed, two of them exchanged glances and giggled before one deliberately tripped him. Jonathan fell to the ground, quickly jumped up, and lunged toward the boy, fists raised. From a short distance away, Gordon Ngubene shouted, 'Jonathan,' and the boy froze. Jonathan stood panting, his face flushed with anger, then turned and walked swiftly toward the school gate without speaking.
related_events: Students harass Jonathan and one trips him
Jonathan reacts aggressively after being tripped
Gordon Ngubene calls out to Jonathan to stop
related_occasions: Dan Pienaar School Athletics Event

name: Jonathan Walks Out After Being Tripped
description: After a group of students laughed and pushed each other near him, one of them tripped Jonathan, causing him to fall. He jumped up, ready to fight, but his father, Gordon, shouted his name. Jonathan stopped, breathing heavily, his face filled with anger. Headmaster Mrs. Cloete watched from nearby but did not intervene. Without saying a word, Jonathan turned and walked quickly toward the school gate. Gordon called out, 'U ya phi?', but Jonathan only glanced back before continuing on his way.
related_events: Mrs. Cloete observes the altercation without intervening
Jonathan storms off toward the school gate in anger
Gordon shouts at Jonathan asking where he is going
related_occasions: Dan Pienaar School Athletics Event

name: Lewinson Takes First Steps in the Jonathan Ngubene Case
description: The coffee girl enters Lewinson's office, places a cup on his desk, and leaves. Lewinson picks up the phone and speaks to Susan, assuring her he will get on it straight away. He laughs, saying he thinks better in the morning, that after lunch he’s a zombie. He hangs up, presses his intercom, and calls for Freda. He tells her to open an account for Benjamin Du Toit, with Jonathan Ngubene as the subject.
related_events: Lewinson makes phone call to Susan
Lewinson instructs Freda to open an account

name: Lewinson Drafts Letter to Police Commissioner
description: Lewinson sits at his desk and types a formal letter on his firm's letterhead. The letter is addressed to the Commissioner of Police at Police Headquarters, John Vorster Square. He writes on behalf of Gordon Ngubene, inquiring about the whereabouts of his son, Jonathan Ngubene. The letter is dated and prepared for dispatch.
related_events: Lewinson drafts letter to Commissioner of Police
Lewinson continues drafting legal correspondence about Jonathan Ngubene

name: The Police Letter
description: Lewinson's letter reaches the police headquarters, and a clerk begins typing a response. The typewriter keys pause, trembling for several seconds, as if uncertain or unwilling. Finally, the letter is completed: a formal note addressed to Lewinson & Partners, stating that they should take the matter up directly with the particular officer in charge. No further information is provided.
related_events: Police respond to Lewinson's inquiry with deflection
Police typewriter hesitates before responding to inquiry about Jonathan Ngubene

name: The Search for Jonathan Ngubene
description: Wellington sits alone in a police interrogation room, flinching at the sounds of moaning and screams coming through the walls. At a Johannesburg hospital, a young black nurse walks down a corridor carrying bedding when she is startled by a screaming, moaning boy being rushed on a trolley into a private ward; a policeman takes position outside the room. Meanwhile, at John Vorster Square, an elderly black cleaner empties garbage at the back of the building. He is shown a photograph of Jonathan Ngubene, looks at it, nods, and silently points downward, indicating the basement.
related_events: Wellington held in police interrogation room
Injured boy admitted to private hospital ward under police guard
Elderly black cleaner identifies Jonathan Ngubene's photograph at police headquarters

name: Matron and Superintendent Deny Jonathan's Presence
description: Gordon and Emily approach the matron, who shakes her head vigorously, denying any knowledge of Jonathan Ngubene and showing them the door. At the same hospital, the white superintendent faces the Julius superintendent, his voice rising in anger. He insists he would have known if Jonathan had been treated there, calls the accusation preposterous, and accuses the other man of raking up trouble.
related_events: Matron denies knowledge of Jonathan Ngubene to Gordon and Emily
White hospital superintendent confronts Julius superintendent over Jonathan Ngubene case

name: Ben Tends to Jonathan's Injuries
description: Ben looked at the six blood-streaked gashes on Jonathan's buttocks, his expression tightening with shock. Without speaking, he reached for tape and carefully applied it to a wound on Jonathan's head. Jonathan flinched as he pulled his shorts back up, wincing at the pain, his face flushed with humiliation. Gordon stood nearby, his voice rising with anger as he insisted his son had done nothing wrong. Ben handed Johan a bottle of iodine, telling him to apply it to the wounds. Susan appeared at the door, then ushered Johan outside as Ben remained with Gordon and his son.
related_events: Ben examines Gordon's son's injuries
Ben applies tape to Jonathan's head injury
Jonathan pulls up his shorts in pain and distress

name: Gordon Confronts Ben About Jonathan's Punishment
description: Gordon stands with Ben, his voice strained as he insists his son Jonathan did nothing wrong. He says the punishment was unjust, that no one listened to the boy, and that he believes Jonathan completely. Ben responds with sympathy but offers little reassurance, suggesting there is nothing they can do now. Gordon presses that he fears the consequences of a police record, not the physical wounds, which he says will heal. He strikes his chest, saying the real injury is the injustice that lingers. Outside, Johan peers through the half-open door, watching silently before being called away. Ben sends Johan to fetch iodine, which he hands to Gordon, telling him to apply it to the wounds on Jonathan’s buttocks.
related_events: Gordon protests his son's unjust punishment
Ben expresses doubt and helplessness

name: Gordon Fears the Lasting Mark of a Police Record
description: Gordon stands with Ben, his voice heavy as he speaks about his son Jonathan. He says he is not worried about the wounds on Jonathan's body, but about what might follow him for life—a police record. He explains that such a mark could make it hard for Jonathan to find work in the future. Ben listens and replies that the case is minor, assuring Gordon there will likely be no record. He tells Gordon not to worry, that it won’t follow the boy.
related_events: Gordon expresses concern about his son's future police record
Ben reassures Gordon about the lack of a police record

name: Gordon Slaps His Chest
description: Gordon stands in the room, his voice rising as he speaks to Ben. He insists his son did nothing wrong and that no one would listen. After Ben suggests the matter is closed, Gordon slaps his chest hard, pointing to his heart. He says he is not worried about the wounds on Jonathan's body, but about the wound inside him—the injustice that will not heal. His face tightens as he repeats the word 'injustice,' letting it hang in the air.
related_events: Gordon emphasizes emotional pain over physical injury

name: Johan Witnesses the Aftermath
description: Johan stands outside, peering through the half-opened door, his face registering shock at the sight of Jonathan's blood-stained buttocks and the visible wounds from the caning. Susan appears at the doorway, calls out to Ben, then gently guides Johan away from the door, leading him back outside.
related_events: Johan witnesses the aftermath through the door
Susan appears at the door and ushers Johan away

name: Ben Sends Johan for Iodine, Medicine Applied to Jonathan's Wounds
description: Ben called Johan from outside and told him to get iodine from the cupboard. Johan rushed into the house and returned with a small bottle of medicine. Ben took it and handed it to Gordon, telling him to rub it on Jonathan's wounds to help them heal.
related_events: Ben instructs Johan to retrieve iodine from the cupboard
Johan retrieves a bottle of medicine from the house
Ben advises Gordon to apply medicine to Jonathan's wounds

name: Minister Bester Greets Parishioners After Service
description: The music stops. The church doors open. Minister Bester, forty years old, stands at the entrance and greets his parishioners as they file out of the church. He exchanges words with them, nodding and smiling as they pass. Among the congregation, Ben Du Toit walks out with his wife Susan and their son Johan. Susan, neatly dressed and composed, greets friends and pauses for brief conversations. Johan, a blond, blue-eyed fourteen-year-old, glances toward a girl his age who is leaving with her parents. She smiles at him; he waves awkwardly. Suzette, Ben’s daughter, stands by a car where a black nanny waits holding a baby. Suzette takes the child, cradles it briefly, then hands it back as the baby begins to wail. She rocks the infant at arm’s length before passing it to the nanny. Ben speaks with a woman, Mrs. Coetzee, who appears drawn and troubled. She tells him her son won’t come to church or school, that he stays in bed all day listening to music. Ben offers to visit him, and she thanks him. Susan calls out to Ben, waving. He returns to her, and she leads him to the car, touching his arm affectionately as they go.
related_events: Minister Bester greets parishioners after church service
related_occasions: Church Service Led By Dominee Bester

name: Susan Greets Friends After Church
description: After the service ends and the congregation leaves the church, Susan Du Toit stops to speak with friends and acquaintances. She exchanges polite words and brief greetings, smiling and nodding as the group disperses. The conversations are short, composed of familiar pleasantries, as people linger momentarily in the churchyard before heading to their cars.
related_events: Susan Du Toit exchanges formalities with friends and acquaintances
related_occasions: Church Service Led By Dominee Bester

name: Johan Waves to the Girl After Church
description: As the parishioners filed out of the church, Johan Du Toit noticed a girl his age. She smiled at him from a distance. He waved back awkwardly. She got into a car with her parents and drove away.

description: Suzette takes her baby from the black nanny waiting by the car and carries the child over to her husband Chris, who is standing with a group of people. She holds the baby up proudly, showing it to those around her. The baby begins to wail, crying loudly. Suzette rocks the child back and forth, holding it at arm's length, but is unable to quiet it. The nanny steps forward, and Suzette hands the baby over.

description: After the church service, Ben Du Toit speaks with Mrs. Coetzee, who appears drawn and worried. She tells him her son refuses to go to church and stays in bed all day, listening to music on his headphones. Ben asks if the boy has been absent from school as well. When she confirms, he offers to visit the boy to talk. She thanks him, relieved, and he says he will call to arrange a time. She smiles gratefully. Susan calls Ben over, and he walks back to join his family.

description: At dinner, Chris hands the Rand Daily Mail to Suzette, who holds it and remarks that the kind of journalism it represents does not help the situation. She looks at the reporter’s photograph and comments on her appearance. Then she passes the newspaper to Ben, who takes it and begins to look it over.

Suzette comments on the journalism in the Rand Daily Mail article

name: Susan and Ben Remember Jonathan Ngubene
description: At the dinner table, Susan looks at the newspaper article and says how tragic it is, remembering Jonathan Ngubene as a kind boy who used to play with her son Johan when they were young. Ben agrees, saying Jonathan was well-mannered and recalls that he was bright at school. The others listen as they continue eating, and Chris helps himself to more food while Suzette picks up the newspaper.

Ben affirms Jonathan Ngubene's good character and manners

name: Ben Reacts to the Shooting Report at Dinner
description: Ben reads the article and looks up, stunned. 'My God, one hundred shot! They didn't have to kill them.' Susan responds, 'This bloody Bruwer woman reports one hundred shot, but the radio said only twenty and the police were attacked first.'

name: Chris Defends Force at Family Dinner
description: At dinner, Suzette passes the Rand Daily Mail to Ben after reading an article about Jonathan Ngubene, a fifteen-year-old boy who died in police custody. Chris dismisses the article, saying the newspaper exaggerates and that some people are out of control. He claims force is the only language they understand. Johan, his son, points out that Jonathan was only fifteen, the same age as him, and asks if Chris would use force on him. Chris replies that Johan is not a terrorist, and that those who are would deserve it. Ben, reading further, reacts in shock to the report that one hundred people were shot. Susan counters, saying the radio reported only twenty and claimed the police were attacked first. Suzette suggests that if black people lived in their own areas, like bantustans, there would be no conflict. Johan asks who would do the work if that happened. Suzette ignores the question, telling him to help clear the dishes. Johan stands, smiles at his father, and shrugs as he leaves the table, with Suzette following in irritation.
related_events: Chris expresses belief that force is the only language certain people understand
Johan challenges Chris by comparing Jonathan Ngubene's age to his own
Chris distinguishes Johan from terrorists and justifies violence against them

name: Suzette Suggests Bantustans, Johan Questions Who Would Work
description: During dinner, Suzette remarks that giving black people their own areas, bantustans, would allow them to live with their own kind and prevent conflict, saying everyone would be happy. Johan responds by asking who would do the work if that happened. Suzette looks at him, confused. Johan stands to help clear the dishes, and Susan tells him to come help her. name: Gordon Reads Testimony of Detention
description: Gordon sits at a table in a small, dimly lit room, reading from a handwritten document by the light of an oil lamp. He recounts being taken to a top floor at John Vorster Square, ordered to undress, and beaten with fists and sjamboks. Wellington, sitting beside him, grows increasingly agitated, glancing around the room as if expecting danger. The black cleaner places a hand on Wellington's shoulder in quiet understanding. Gordon continues, describing hours of interrogation by Captain Stolz and other policemen, the repeated beatings, and the suffocating terror of having a wet bag placed over his head. He speaks of hearing Jonathan scream during a beating, followed by the sound of furniture crashing and Stolz shouting at him to get up. Gordon says he later learned Jonathan had been taken to hospital and that he never saw him again. A heavy silence follows. Emily closes her eyes, then begins to sob. Robert stands beside her chair, his face set in anger. Gordon pauses, closes his eyes, and steadies himself. He offers a pen to Wellington, who moves to sign the document, but suddenly stops at the sound of an approaching truck. Wellington rushes to the window, then flees through a bedroom window in panic. Moments later, the front door bursts open. Five policemen enter—two white and three African. The youngest child wakes and cries. Emily picks him up, holds him close, and returns to her seat. Lieutenant Venter orders everyone to stay where they are. He picks up the papers on the table and hands them to Captain Stolz, who enters behind him. Stolz reads the pages silently, folds them, and places them in his jacket pocket. He approaches Gordon and tells him to stand. Gordon remains seated. Stolz turns to the black cleaner, who stands up without being told, and says they know each other.

name: Gordon Offers Pen, Wellington Flees at Sound of Truck
description: Gordon finishes reading the testimony and reaches for a pen, holding it out for Wellington to sign the document at the bottom of the page. Wellington moves toward the pen, but before he can take it, the sound of an approaching truck echoes outside. He flinches, rushes to the front window, peers out, then turns sharply and sprints into a bedroom. A moment later, he jumps through the window and disappears. The room falls into stunned silence.

Five policemen—two white and three African—enter the room. The youngest child stirs from sleep and begins to cry. Emily rises, picks up the child, and returns to her seat. Lieutenant Venter orders everyone to stay where they are. He notices papers on the table, picks them up, and flips through them. Captain Stolz walks in, surveys the room, and takes the papers from Venter. He reads them silently, folds them, and places them in his jacket pocket. He steps toward Gordon and demands he stand. Gordon remains silent. Stolz turns to the black cleaner, who stands up. Stolz says, "We know each other, don't we?" and begins to pace around him.

Lieutenant Venter reports that nothing has been found. Stolz ignores the report and commands that Gordon and the black cleaner be taken away. The two men are handcuffed. As they are led out by the security police, Gordon turns and gives Emily a final look before disappearing into the night.

name: Student Leader Initiates Protest March at Orlando Secondary School
description: At Orlando Secondary School, a student leader steps forward and calls for silence. The students immediately stop talking and turn to listen. He speaks to them, and they respond by shouting slogans: 'No to Bantu education,' 'No to apartheid,' and 'Freedom Now.' After the speeches, the students begin to march out of the school grounds. They carry banners that read 'No to the Oppressor's language' and 'Bantu education is slave education.' Others hold signs that say 'EQUAL EDUCATION NOW,' 'ONE MAN ONE VOTE,' and 'FREE OUR LEADERS.' As they move through the school yard and onto the street, they sing freedom songs, their voices loud and steady. Jonathan and Wellington walk among them, singing along. More students join the march from side streets, forming a larger group as they head toward the main road.

name: Students Join March at Crossroad and Raise Voices in Protest
description: Jonathan's group of students turned onto a main street where several other groups were already gathering. More students arrived from different directions, joining the growing crowd. Banners reading 'EQUAL EDUCATION NOW,' 'ONE MAN ONE VOTE,' and 'NO TO THE AFRIKAANS LANGUAGE' were held high as the march swelled in size. The students began chanting: 'If we learn Afrikaans, Vorster must learn Zulu,' followed by 'Bantu education! Stinks! Stinks! Stinks!' and 'Equal education! Now! Now! Now!' They sang freedom songs in unison, their voices rising together as they moved forward along the road.

name: Students Sing 'Nkosi Sikelele' as Police Block March
description: The march approaches a barricade of three police jeeps blocking the street, with troop carriers parked further behind. Camouflaged police officers, including six dog handlers, stand across the road, their dogs straining at the leashes. The Soweto police Commandant steps forward with a loudspeaker and orders the students to disperse, declaring the demonstration illegal. The students do not stop. Instead, they begin singing 'Nkosi Sikelele,' the African national anthem, their voices rising in unison. Young children, some as young as eight or nine, sing with clenched fists held high, alongside older students like Jonathan and Wellington. The police, now wearing gas masks, receive signals from a junior officer and move forward with tear gas canisters. The singing continues, steady and loud, as the tension builds.

description: After the Commandant issues a final warning for the crowd to disperse, a voice in the group shouts 'Bantu education...' and the students immediately respond with 'Stinks, Stinks, Stinks!' The chanting rises from the crowd, steady and loud. In response, the police begin moving forward, carrying tear gas canisters. They pull on their gas masks, adjusting their grips on the canisters as they prepare to act. The tension builds between the two groups, the air thick with anticipation as the officers take their positions at the front lines.

name: Students Flee and Fight Back After Police Attack
description: Tear gas canisters exploded into the crowd, and the dog handlers lunged forward, releasing the dogs. Students scattered in all directions, many coughing and clutching their faces as smoke filled the air. Amid the chaos, some of the students began hurling stones at the police line. One stone struck an officer in the face, drawing blood, and he was helped away by a Black policeman. The singing had stopped, replaced by shouts, cries, and the sharp sounds of stones hitting metal and flesh.

name: Jonathan and Wellington Help the Wounded Amid Police Violence
description: The police opened fire on the students as they scattered in all directions. Screams filled the air as children and teenagers fell to the ground. A little girl collapsed, shot in the back as she ran. Smoke rose from a burning car and a nearby building engulfed in flames. Amid the chaos, a woman rushed out of a house, grabbing two young children and pulling them to safety. Bystanders darted through the smoke, trying to reach the injured. Jonathan knelt beside a wounded girl, shouting for Wellington to help. Wellington turned back and ran to them, helping lift the girl. A seventeen-year-old girl stepped forward, facing two policemen, shouting that they should shoot her too. Police officers pushed Jonathan, Wellington, and the injured girl into a van. As the van drove off, they left the girl behind on the road, motionless. Neighbors ran out, gathering around her, trying to help. Police dismounted from troop carriers and chased after fleeing students. Some boys picked up dustbin lids, using them as shields while hurling stones at the officers. A police jeep screeched around the corner, blocking the escape route of a fleeing group. Ambulance sirens wailed in the distance, barely audible over the noise. The streets of Soweto lay scattered with the dead and wounded. Officers stood still, their faces blank, as smoke curled into the sky.

They shook hands, and Viljoen welcomed him warmly, mentioning that he had once watched Ben play rugby for the Transvaal. Ben smiled and acknowledged it had been a long time. A knock came at the door, and Captain Stolz stepped in. Viljoen introduced him, and Stolz gave a formal nod before shaking Ben's hand. description: Ben meets with Colonel Viljoen and speaks on behalf of Gordon Ngubene, explaining that he knows him well from their time working together at the school. He suggests there may have been a misunderstanding and offers to help clear things up. Ben describes Gordon as an honest, hard-working, and churchgoing man, someone who would not get involved in any kind of trouble. He emphasizes his long-standing relationship with Gordon and expresses confidence that he is not the kind of person they are looking for.

name: Viljoen Defends the Investigation
description: Colonel Viljoen sits behind his desk and tells Ben that the inquiry into Gordon Ngubene is routine, part of the necessary work of investigating township matters thoroughly. He leans back in his chair and speaks about the challenges the police face, mentioning the intense criticism from the press, especially English newspapers. He scoffs at their complaints, saying they will be the first to flee the country if there is any real danger. He warns of the threat posed by communists and insists the police have a duty to follow every lead. Ben listens and tries to assure him that Gordon is not involved in anything dangerous, but Viljoen remains firm, emphasizing the importance of leaving no stone unturned.

name: Ben Defends Gordon Ngubene
description: Ben tells Colonel Viljoen that he fully supports the police and their work. He says he believes Gordon Ngubene is innocent and may have been wrongly included in the investigation. Ben adds that everyone makes mistakes. Viljoen laughs and agrees, saying people often forget that even officials are human.

Ben hesitates, then responds by asking the Colonel how he would feel if it were his own son. The room falls silent. Captain Stolz, standing by the window, interrupts to state that the information was already provided. Ben turns slightly, showing surprise at Stolz’s remark. description: Viljoen leans forward, asking if grief could drive a man to destructive acts, and wonders aloud why there is resistance when the government has provided so much. He looks directly at Ben and asks whether people like him truly stand with the government or not. Ben stiffens, his voice tightening as he says he feels accused. Viljoen raises a hand, offering a quick smile. He says he didn’t mean to offend—it’s just the way things are said in the course of duty. The room grows lighter. Ben chuckles, then both men laugh, the sound filling the space between them. Satisfied, Viljoen pushes back his chair and stands. Outside, the distant hum of the station resumes.
